body: Please do not bind new lsp endpoints, they should not be a public API and there is no technical reason for it anymore. See https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/105016

This has nothing to do with the linked issue. Also this is the wrong place to do this, it mixes up the cache for client managed files with file system observation. These have nothing to with each other and clients must properly open and close files when renaming them. `didDeleteFiles` has the same problem see https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/105236
We should not rely on a uid file existing and since there is no `ignoreIfNotExists` flag, we should check this on our end.

I think it is important to strictly separate between normative comments and non normative comments. The documentation comments in this file are all from the spec. If we want implementation notes, we should move them to a separate comment IMO.
Why add this as variable, it makes the struct bigger and is never used. We can just embed the kind into the serialization function.
At the moment this file is not a full model of the LSP types. It only models what we actually use. We don't use or support annotationId so there is no need to have it in our model.

The type of options is `options?: CreateFileOptions`, `null` does not fit that type, so if `options` is `null` we should not add the key to the dictionary. (Note the difference between `undefined` and `null` in typescript which is used for the lsp spec)

Which style should be used for the separate comment?

I think I misunderstood what the script cache is doing here. It's true that clients close and open files when renaming, so the parsing of the next one should happen on it's own.

I removed this completely. Let me know if you have further suggestions related to this
Removing it from this PR seems the right thing to do. If there are problems with the current reload behaviour when renaming, it's a different bug that we can address in another PR.

To cite the spec:

> The will delete files request is sent from the client to the server

This is no notification nor is it send by the server. We must respond to the request sent by the client, we do this by returning the result from the callback. Json rpc will wrap the returned result into a [jsonrpc result object](https://www.jsonrpc.org/specification#response_object) and will send it to the client.

There are cases where falling back to `Variant` to represent union types makes sense. But for nullable booleans I think we can just keep it a boolean since there should be no difference in behaviour between `undefined` and `false`.
